patterns: is a hypothesis the same as a theory
entries.answer: A hypothesis is a testable proposed answer, and the word carries the requirement that evidence could count against it. A statement that cannot be falsified is not a weak hypothesis, it is not one, which is the most common way first research goes wrong. The useful discipline is to write the null alongside it, and the surprising part is how often people cannot state the null, which means they have not thought about what would show them to be wrong.

patterns: what are the limits of peer review
entries.answer: Peer review is assessment of research by others in the same field who are not the author, and it is the main quality control on published work. What it reliably catches is error, bad method and unsupported claims; what it does not catch is a well-executed study of an uninteresting question. It is also incomplete as a system: review is usually done by a small number of people, sometimes by someone whose own work is being reviewed, and it checks the argument rather than the honesty of the data.

entries.answer: Citation bias is the tendency for studies with striking results to be cited more often than careful ones, and it has a measurable effect on what a field believes. Positive results get published and negative ones do not, which is the related problem called publication bias, and together they make the literature read as if every treatment works. The countermeasure is a systematic review protocol, which fixes the question and the search before the results are known and so cannot be quietly adjusted afterwards.

patterns: why do scientists care about replication
entries.answer: Reproducibility is the degree to which somebody else can repeat a result from what was written down, and it is now treated as a minimum rather than an achievement. It fails for mundane reasons most of the time: missing detail in the method, data held privately, and software that no longer runs. The last is why specifying versions is part of the method and not a footnote, since an analysis rerun on a current version of a library may not produce the published number.

patterns: what does a methodology section contain
entries.answer: Methodology is the part of a study that describes how the work was done rather than what it found, and it is the section readers skip and the one that determines whether they can trust the result. It has to cover sampling, how data was collected, how it was analysed, and what was excluded, and the exclusions are the part that most often contains a choice made after seeing the data. Methodology is also where a study's limits are declared, and a paper without them is usually hiding something.
